page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Below the text, centred: the heading "EXERC. X." and a title in italic capitals and italic. Then a new paragraph with a large initial Q. Small "»" marks stand at the right edge beside the lines of that paragraph. Gathering signature "C 5" at the lower left, with the catchword "subiun-" at the lower right.

main_text.p: enim soles, quot corpora, in quae agit, ipse produceret. Sic neq; ignis lignu, quod urit, in sui naturam, sed in cinere mutat. Calcearius item corium in quod agit, in se nequaquam uertit. Sunt (ut summatim dicam ) & alia pene innumera agentia, quae sua in se nō uertunt subiecta. Igitur hoc Fernelij effatum, nō simpliciter, sed distinctè, & quatenus fieri potest, intelligitur. Nam agens naturale subiectum, quod quidem est hoc fieri natum aptum, in quod agit, conuertit. Panis utiq; in sanguinem ab animalis calore, deinde in carne mutari potest: quoniam ille est caro potentia, hoc est, potentiam in se habet, per quam a naturali calore sic mutari potest. Quoniam autem hac potestate carent lapides, ideo nulla caloris animalis ui in sanguinem, ac tandem in carnem conuerti queunt.
main_text.head: EXERC. X.

head.i: AN SVBSTANTIALIS FORMA A' subiecto extrinsecus assumatur ?

main_text.p: QVæ postea subdit Fernelius capite eodem, nempe substantialem forma extrinsecus assumi a subiecto, cum ijs cohaerere non uidentur, quae mox

page.notes: The "»" marks at the right edge beside the lines "forma extrinsecus assumi a subiecto, cum ijs cohaerere non uidentur" are not printed text, so they are left out. The heading mark "A'" is read as an apostrophe with [?] omitted, as it is clearly printed. Long s has been rendered as s throughout, so "eft" appears as "est" and "fubiecto" as "subiecto". The printed "fui" in line 3 is read as "sui" and the "s" forms in the heading follow the same rule. The printed "nó" is read as "nō" with a macron. No other doubtful readings.
